title: Chosen local module isomorphisms transport uniquely with adjunction-unit normalization
statement: Let $C,D$ be small sites with finite limits [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], topologies $J,K$, and a continuous finite-limit-preserving functor $F:C\to D$. Let $R,S$ be ring sheaves, $\rho:R\to F_*S$, and use the existing module inverse-image adjunction [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $A,G$ be $R$-module sheaves, $B,P$ be $S$-module sheaves, $c:F^*A\simeq B$, $b:P\simeq F^*G$, $V\in C$, and $e:G|_V\simeq A|_V$ on the localized site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. There is a unique isomorphism $d:P|_{F(V)}\simeq B|_{F(V)}$ such that for every $W\to V$ and $x\in G(W)$, $d(b^{-1}(\eta_G(x)))=\operatorname{adj}(c)(e(x))$ on $F(W)\to F(V)$, where $\eta$ is the specified module pullback unit. No condition of commutativity, finiteness, or constant coefficients is needed for the ring sheaves.

proof.text: Let F_V be Over.post F at V and restrict rho componentwise to define its scalar map. Continuity follows from covering preservation and flatness, since F_V preserves finite limits. Product preservation identifies F followed by Over.star(F V) with Over.star V followed by F_V. The product comparison and naturality of rho give an isomorphism between the two module direct-image composites.

proof.text: Compose the inverse-image adjunction with restriction/right-extension adjunctions, transport its right adjoint through this direct-image isomorphism, and cancel the restriction adjunction on the source. This gives a bijection Hom((F*G)|F(V),Q) = Hom(G|V,(F_V)*Q), natural in Q. Expand the units and counit: at W the resulting map sends x to z(eta_G(x)); the product-comparison projection equations and naturality cancel the auxiliary product restriction. Keep this hom equivalence irreducible and use its sectionwise computation and naturality lemmas as the proof API, preventing repeated expansion of the composed adjunctions.

proof.text: Under this bijection let z correspond to e followed by the image of c|F(V). Precomposition by z is bijective on Hom into every Q, because both hom equivalences and precomposition by e and c are bijective. The coyoneda criterion makes z an isomorphism. Conjugate by b|F(V) to get d. The computed unit formula gives normalization, and injectivity of the hom equivalence gives uniqueness. The normalized equation is named NormalizedLocalModuleTrivialization and reused verbatim by the scheme-site specialization, preventing repeated scalar-restriction expansion.

theorem normalized_local_module_pullback
    {C D : Type u} [SmallCategory C] [SmallCategory D]
    [HasFiniteLimits C] [HasFiniteLimits D]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D)
    (F : C ⥤ D) [F.IsContinuous J K] [PreservesFiniteLimits F]
    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} {S : Sheaf K RingCat.{u}}
    (rho : R ⟶ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).obj S)
    (A G : SheafOfModules.{u} R) (B P : SheafOfModules.{u} S)
    (c : (pullback rho).obj A ≅ B) (b : P ≅ (pullback rho).obj G)
    (V : C) (e : G.over V ≅ A.over V) :
    NormalizedLocalModuleTrivialization J K F rho A G B P c.hom b V e
